title: RE-Bench Is a Systems Benchmark: What Its Scorers and Selection Rules Actually Support
description:
This version-bounded technical note examines what RE-Bench (Research Engineering Benchmark, V1) directly measures and which inferences its scores can support. It treats the evaluated unit as a complete agent system—including the model, scaffold, tools, execution environment, feedback surface, hardware, time budget, attempt allocation, and selector—rather than as a base model in isolation.

The review keeps two evidence surfaces separate: results and methods reported in the historical RE-Bench paper, and properties of the public implementation at pinned METR/RE-Bench commit 93b98062e55f6945d4a7e213a3226dd419896170. All seven task packages at that revision were statically inspected. A published eight-test harness additionally checks bounded behaviors in four hash-pinned files across Optimize a Kernel, Scaling Law Experiment, and Optimize LLM Foundry.

The three detailed cases illustrate distinct measurement boundaries: selected single-call timing and public contract drift in Kernel; a static eleven-point evaluator and one-sided FLOP gate in Scaling Law; and a declared L1 quantity implemented as a sum of per-tensor norms in LLM Foundry, where parameter proximity remains narrower than behavioral equivalence. The note also distinguishes paper-level score@k selection from single-run reliability, within-run aggregation, and an agent's ability to identify its own best artifact.

This is an unaffiliated, AI-assisted pinned-source contract audit. It is not peer reviewed, independently adjudicated, or an independent benchmark-hardware or headline-result reproduction. Exact mapping between the pinned source and the historical paper-run environments remains unresolved; consequently, the review makes no claim that the identified source properties changed, invalidated, or explain any historical leaderboard result.

additional_description.title: Status and assistance disclosure
additional_description.text:
This record is a public working review, version 0.1. Research synthesis, source navigation, comparison, contract-test development, and drafting were AI-assisted under human direction. AI-generated interpretation was not treated as evidence: central implementation claims are scoped to identified source files, pinned hashes, or bounded executable checks.

The record has not undergone peer review or independent human adjudication. The executable checks are source-contract tests only; they do not execute a participant submission, protected scorer service, H100 benchmark workload, model trajectory, official solution archive, or RE-Bench headline-result reproduction.

The exact identity relationship between the pinned public source and the environments used for the historical paper results has not been established. Pinned-source findings are therefore not transferred retrospectively to the reported runs, and this record makes no claim that a historical leaderboard result changed, was invalid, or was exploit-driven. Independent review remains welcome as a future assurance upgrade.
